labs.title: Create a Microsoft Purview DLP policy in simulation mode
labs.summary: Use a simulated Microsoft Purview portal to create a DLP policy for credit card data shared externally across Microsoft 365.
labs.scenario: Contoso wants to test a DLP policy before enforcement. In the **simulated Microsoft Purview portal**, create a policy for **Data stored in connected sources** that detects **Credit Card Number** content shared with people outside the organization. Scope it to **Exchange email**, **SharePoint sites**, **OneDrive accounts**, and **Teams chat and channel messages**. Configure the action to block only external recipients, show policy tips, create high-severity alerts, and run in **simulation mode** first.
learningObjectives: Create a Microsoft Purview DLP policy from an enterprise data protection scenario
Configure sensitive information conditions, locations, notifications, and incident reports
Choose simulation mode before enforcement to reduce business disruption
prerequisites: Know that DLP policies identify, monitor, and protect sensitive information across Microsoft 365 locations.

actions.title: DLP policy created
actions.message: Simulation data is available for review.

components.text: Simulation mode audits matches and can show policy tips without enforcing the block. Review results before enforcement.

**Why simulation mode first?** A DLP policy has three rollout controls: state, scope, and action impact. In this lab the rule is intentionally strong: it detects high-confidence Credit Card Number matches when content is shared externally, then prepares a block for external recipients. Running in simulation mode lets administrators review Exchange, SharePoint, OneDrive, and Teams matches, confirm the rule is not catching normal business content, and educate users with policy tips before enforcement. This is different from a sensitivity label: the label classifies and protects an item, while DLP evaluates user activity and sharing context so the service can audit, warn, alert, or block risky disclosure. When Contoso is ready to enforce, the same policy can be tuned and then changed from simulation to on, but that is deliberately outside this first pilot.

The seeded matches model a realistic pilot: a spreadsheet in SharePoint, an Exchange message, a OneDrive document, and a Teams conversation each contain a fictional credit card pattern and are shared with a fictional external recipient. The correct response in this lab is not to delete the content or enable every location; it is to define a measurable control, scope it to the required Microsoft 365 locations, show users policy tips, and give admins high-severity alerts they can investigate before production enforcement.

This reinforces the SC-900 distinction between information protection controls, which travel with labeled content, and DLP controls, which evaluate locations, conditions, user actions, notifications, alerts, and deployment state. The learner also sees why choosing **Turn it on right away** is risky when stakeholders have asked for a monitored pilot rather than immediate enforcement.
Do not switch to enforcement until stakeholders review false positives and user impact.
Activity explorer would show audited DLP activity for simulation mode.

steps.instruction: Choose **Data stored in connected sources**, select **Financial** and **U.S. Financial Data**, then name the policy **Protect credit card data shared externally**.

labs.solution:
1. Go to **Data Loss Prevention** > **Policies** > **+ Create policy**.
2. Choose **Data stored in connected sources**, category **Financial**, template **U.S. Financial Data**.
3. Name the policy `Protect credit card data shared externally` and keep **Admin units** as **Full directory**.
4. Select **Exchange email**, **SharePoint sites**, **OneDrive accounts**, and **Teams chat and channel messages** only.
5. Select **Credit Card Number**, set **Instance count** to `1`, **Confidence level** to **High confidence**, turn on the external sharing condition, and choose **Block only people outside your organization**.
6. Turn on **User notifications**, set **Incident report severity** to **High**, turn on admin alerts, choose **Run the policy in simulation mode**, turn on **Show policy tips while in simulation mode**, and select **Submit**.
7. Open the policy and select **View simulation results**.
